verdict.rationale: Unity documents running the Editor and Player from the command line to automate workflows, including a headless Player mode. A first-party Unity CLI is aimed at CI and build agents, with headless-worker distribution, JSON output and exit codes, and Unity Build Automation provides hosted CI for multiplatform builds. Missing for 10: no independent hands-on report of a headless CI run succeeding, and the Editor's -batchmode/-nographics flags are only referenced via a probe rather than quoted from the docs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: You can launch the Unity Editor and Player with additional command line arguments to control startup behavior, configure settings, or automate workflows.
Run the application in headless mode. In this mode, the application doesn’t display anything or accept user input.
The Unity CLI works well for: Continuous integration (CI) and build agents where installing the full Hub is undesirable.
Use Unity Build Automation and its continuous integration features for multiplatform builds.
the entry point to the editor whose -batchmode/-nographics CLI is documented for headless CI builds.
